sentences.text: Applicant :- Udai Chand Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Gorakh Nath Mourya Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.

Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
None has appeared for informant.

2. This bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in case crime No. 319 of 2020,
under Sections-498A, 304B IPC and Sections-3 / 4 of D. P. Act, police station Saini, District Kaushambi, with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
Applicant is husband of deceased.
Marriage of deceased with applicant has taken place one year prior to the incident.
Allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased levelled against the applicant, are wholly false.

It was submitted that after Udai Chand vs State Of U.P. on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56778049/
1 two days of the incident, informant had made a complaint to the police, on which, first information report was lodged, wherein, only general allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased were levelled.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Later on, the informant has submitted another tehrir before the police, wherein, he has changed the version and made false allegation that the applicant was having illicit relations with his sister-in-law.
It is further submitted that the applicant was doing business of cloths and on the day of incident he was not present on the spot.
Lastly, it was submitted that the applicant is in jail since 30.7.2020 and that in case he is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the applicant is husband of deceased.
In post-mortem report, five injuries have been shown on the body of the deceased and cause of death of deceased is ante mortem throttling, which suggests that the deceased suffered homicidal death.
The applicant has failed to offer any plausible explanation as to how his wife (deceased) has suffered injuries and died.

5. Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, I do not find it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
6. Accordingly, this bail application moved on behalf of the applicant Udai Chand is rejected.

7. However, considering the period of detention of the applicant, the concerned trial court is directed to expedite the trial and conclude the same as early as possible, preferably within a period of ten months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
Order Date :- 16.4.2024 HR
